body_markdown:
# Introduction

Knowing workplace vocabulary helps you communicate with colleagues, supervisors, customers and visitors. This lesson covers common office places, people, equipment, documents and actions.

## 1. People at work

- Employee — The employee arrived on time.
- Employer — The employer provides the equipment.
- Manager — Please speak to the manager.
- Supervisor — The supervisor checks the work.
- Colleague — My colleague helped me.
- Receptionist — The receptionist answered the phone.
- Customer — The customer asked a question.
- Client — We have a meeting with a client.
- Applicant — The applicant submitted a form.
- Team — Our team works together.

## 2. Office places

- Office — I work in an office.
- Reception — Please wait at the reception.
- Meeting room — The meeting is in the meeting room.
- Cabin — The manager is in the cabin.
- Workplace — Keep your workplace clean.
- Branch — Our branch is near the station.
- Entrance — Use the main entrance.
- Exit — The emergency exit is on the left.
- Pantry — The pantry is on this floor.
- Storage room — Keep the files in the storage room.

## 3. Office equipment

- Computer — Turn on the computer.
- Laptop — I use a laptop for work.
- Keyboard — The keyboard is not working.
- Mouse — Move the mouse carefully.
- Printer — The printer needs paper.
- Scanner — Scan the document.
- Photocopier — Make two copies on the photocopier.
- Telephone — The telephone is ringing.
- Projector — Connect the laptop to the projector.
- Stapler — Use a stapler to attach the pages.

## 4. Documents and administration

- Form — Fill in this form.
- Application — Your application is under review.
- Report — Submit the report today.
- Register — Write the details in the register.
- File — Keep the file safely.
- Invoice — The invoice has been sent.
- Receipt — Please keep the receipt.
- Notice — Read the notice carefully.
- Schedule — Check the work schedule.
- Attendance — Mark your attendance.

## 5. Common workplace actions

- Attend — I attend the meeting every Monday.
- Arrange — Arrange the documents in order.
- Approve — The manager approved the request.
- Assign — The supervisor assigned a task.
- Check — Please check the details.
- Complete — Complete the work before lunch.
- Discuss — We will discuss the issue.
- Inform — Inform the team about the change.
- Prepare — Prepare the meeting notes.
- Submit — Submit the form by Friday.

## 6. Useful workplace expressions

- Could you please explain this task?
- I have completed the report.
- May I speak to the supervisor?
- The printer is not working.
- I will send the document by email.
- Could you repeat the instructions?
- I need a little more time.
- The meeting has been postponed.
- Please confirm the schedule.
- Thank you for your support.

## 7. Common mistakes

- Incorrect: I am working in office. Correct: I am working in an office.
- Incorrect: Discuss about the issue. Correct: Discuss the issue.
- Incorrect: Please revert back. More natural: Please reply.
- Incorrect: I have submitted yesterday. Correct: I submitted it yesterday.

## Practice

Choose the correct word.

1. A person who manages a team is a ___. (manager / customer)
2. We print a document using a ___. (printer / keyboard)
3. Write your name on this ___. (form / mouse)
4. Please ___ the report before Friday. (submit / reception)
5. The team will ___ the problem. (discuss / invoice)

**Answers:** 1. manager, 2. printer, 3. form, 4. submit, 5. discuss.

## Speaking practice

Describe your workplace in five sentences. Mention the people, equipment, tasks and one thing you do every day. Example: “I work in an office. My supervisor assigns daily tasks. I use a computer and telephone. I check the documents. I submit my report before leaving.”

## Learning tip

Choose five words from your actual workplace each day. Use each word in a sentence and try to use those sentences during real conversations.

faq.question: What is the difference between an employee and an employer?
faq.answer: An employee works for an organisation or person. An employer hires employees and provides work.

faq.question: What does submit mean?
faq.answer: Submit means to formally give or send something for consideration, approval or record.

faq.question: How can I improve workplace English?
faq.answer: Learn words connected with your actual tasks and practise polite, short sentences every day.
